props.source: real (OSM node 14068526388, where a crossing way meets barrier=kerb way 1546755070 tagged tactile_paving=yes): the surveyed curb ramp. One pad per attach node, so two crossings meeting at one node render as the single shared ramp they are. Approximation: pad size is a standard one.

confirmed (louellen_st_west/w_broad_st_southwest corner - Signalization confirmed from OSM: node 104043149 at this exact junction is tagged highway=traffic_signals, traffic_signals:direction=both, and the Louellen St crossing (way 376498339 / node 3674859831) is crossing=traffic_signals with button_operated=no and crossing:island=no - a signalised crossing on automatic recall, no pushbutton, no refuge island. That is real surveyed third-party data, NOT a field survey and NOT a street-view review by us. What is NOT sourced: the pole hardware type above, and the per-corner pedestrian_head placement below.
): full-width mast-arm signal, pole at the real corner-fillet arc midpoint; the arm extends at a right angle to louellen_st_west (parallel to its crosswalk, perpendicular to its travel direction), reaching roughly to mid-roadway (arm_length_ft=9.7, half of louellen_st_west's real curb-to-curb width) - confirmed via street-view against a real example (NW corner's arm over West Broad St), not a diagonal reach toward the intersection center. Exactly which lane the head hangs over isn't surveyed.
